stories.title: Africa's opposition voices face growing pressure
stories.summary: https://p.dw.com/p/5PwH7 Prefer DW on Google The leader of Chadema, Tanzania's main opposition party, was sentenced to four years in prison in November 2026 for incitement to unrest Image: Ericky Boniphace/AFP Advertisement From Cameroon and Tanzania to Mozambique, Nigeria and Zambia, opposition leaders have accused authorities of limiting political freedoms through legal action and restrictions on public activity. In each case, officials have said the measures are justified under national laws and security provisions. " Cameroon is very sensitive, and it is important that we know when to criticize the government and when not to criticize the government openly," said Ngam Glory Ani Mbom, a citizen of the central African country. She said fear of arrest and violence discourage political participation. "You cannot talk about democracy when opposition supporters cannot freely express their minds to the public," she told DW. For Ndah Grimbald, deputy secretary-general of Cameroon's opposition Social Democratic Front, one of the biggest obstacles is organizing public meetings. "The first major challenge we face as members of the opposition is the non-authorization of public rallies, public meetings," he said, noting that opposition proposals receive little attention in parliament. "Private members' bills are not even listened to." Cameroonian law guarantees freedom of assembly but allows authorities to restrict gatherings on grounds of public order or national security. Organizers are also required to notify officials in advance.

stories.summary: Nigeria: Infantino's Snub of Ogborodu, Kebbi FIFA Projects Sparks Stakeholders' Outrage 26 November 2026 Leadership (Abuja) By Salifu Usman Football stakeholders in Nigeria have expressed disappointment that FIFA President Gianni Infantino failed to inspect the long-delayed FIFA Goal Projects at Ogborodu in Delta State and Kebbi State during his recent visit to the country. Infantino was in Nigeria for the 48th Ordinary General Assembly of the Confederation of African Football (CAF) in Abuja but left without visiting the two facilities, whose delayed completion has continued to raise questions over the implementation of FIFA-funded football development projects. stories.title: Tunisia: One Year After Journalist Sonia Dahmani's Release, CPJ Urges Tunisia to Free All Jailed Press

Dahmani was conditionally released on November 27, 2025, after spending more than 18 months behind bars over her media commentary. Despite her release, she continues to face multiple prosecutions and prison sentences under Tunisia's cybercrime Decree-Law 54, leaving her at risk of imprisonment once again. "The release of Sonia Dahmani has not changed the reality facing journalists in Tunisia: reporting critically on those in power can still land you in prison. Journalists remain behind bars, others are handed prison sentences, and the threat of prosecution hangs over anyone who dares to speak out," said CPJ Regional Director Sara Qudah. "Tunisian authorities cannot claim progress on press freedom while using the courts as a weapon against independent journalism. They must free all journalists jailed for their work and end this relentless judicial harassment." Journalists Zied el-Heni, Mourad Zghidi, Borhen Bsaies, and Mohamed Yousfi remain behind bars amid prosecutions involving criminal, financial, and terrorism-related allegations.

The discussions took place at the Ittihadiya Palace in Cairo, where al-Sisi reaffirmed Egypt's support for Sudan and its national institutions amid the devastating consequences of the ongoing war. The combination of challenges has raised questions about whether the government can defend itself against Islamist militant group al-Shabab while managing growing divisions among political factions. Some analysts fear the situation could embolden al-Shabab, which is affiliated with al-Qaeda, and potentially allow it to seize control of the capital, Mogadishu. The group of six tourists, four British, one Swiss and one American, accompanied by local guides, were hiking near the village of Bakingili in the south of the Mount Cameroon national park on 19 November, on a path used by elephants to access a nearby lake, when they encountered the herd of about 15 animals, according to media reports. The elephants attacked the group and Alain Throo, a Swiss insurance executive based in London, was reportedly gored and one of the guides tossed into a ditch on top of Throo, while the others hid in trees. Throo had a black eye and was initially responsive and complaining about an injury to his arm, one of the British female hikers told Cameroonian media, which said they had feared he was bleeding internally. “He said that the elephant attacked him,” an unidentified Cameroonian man added, according to a video posted by CBS Radio Buea FM. “It smashed him.” View image in fullscreen An African forest elephant. Photograph: 2026 Vantor/AP Russian warship sinks in Benghazi after suspected Ukrainian drone attack No one has claimed responsibility for the strike on the vessel, which had docked on its way back to Russia A Russian warship docked in the Libyan port city of Benghazi was struck in the early hours of Sunday in a suspected Ukrainian sea drone attack, causing a dramatic night-time explosion and the sinking of the vessel. The strike severely damaged the Merkury, a Russian navy corvette that had stopped to refuel and take on supplies, according to Libyan officials from the country’s eastern government. Initial reports said several Ukrainian sea drones were launched at the ship.

stories.title: Nigerian youth have shown their power in the past - why aren't they shaping this election?
stories.summary: Image source, AFP via Getty Images Image caption, Bola Tinubu (in red hat) would be 79 at the end of a second term, if he is re-elected By Mansur Abubakar Reporting from Abuja Published 22 November 2026 Abdulhadi Dalhatu is something of a rarity in Nigeria politics. At 38, he is among the young people seeking elected office in a country where about 80% of the population is under 40. He hopes his age will stand in his favour as he campaigns for a seat in the state assembly in the northern Kano state in January's general elections. "Younger people are the majority in this country and should be deciding the future," Dalhatu tells the BBC. But Nigeria's political history suggests he faces an uphill battle. Since the return to civilian rule in 1999, Goodluck Jonathan has been the youngest person elected president, taking office at the age of 53.

stories.title: ANC fights to keep control of South Africa's key cities after election setback
stories.summary: Image source, Gallo Images via Getty Images Image caption, The ANC got the most votes overall but lost control in more than half of the councils it won in 2021 Published 21 November 2026 The party that has dominated South Africa for more than 30 years is in a race against time to secure power-sharing deals in most of the country's cities after a massive drop in its support in this month's local elections. The African National Congress (ANC) suffered its worstâ¯result since it came to power in 1994 when South Africa transitioned from the racist apartheid system to democracy. It won a majority in just one of the country's nine provinces, Limpopo, down from six in the last elections. It won the most votes in just two of the country's eight cities, compared with six in 2021. At the national level, the ANC is sharing power with its long-time rival, the Democratic Alliance (DA), but while there is still no official announcement, it appears that ANC party officials do not want to replicate this at the local level.

In his hospital in Uganda , Dr Eric Wobudeya treats young infants after the virus has attacked their lungs and airways, or triggered pneumonia. “These are children who are dying, and they are struggling for oxygen,” he said. Around the world, children are facing the consequences of low or falling measles vaccination rates.

stories.title: California’s coastal communities on alert as biggest waves in years hit state
stories.summary: People watch a large wave break over the seawall in Pacifica, California Photograph: Fred Greaves/Reuters View image in fullscreen People watch a large wave break over the seawall in Pacifica, California Photograph: Fred Greaves/Reuters California’s coastal communities on alert as biggest waves in years hit state Hazard warnings issued throughout week after powerful swells and waves of more than 9 metres recorded Multiple coastal hazard warnings were issued this week across California as successive areas of low pressure generated powerful swells and large breaking waves for coastal communities. Beaches and piers were closed last weekend as large waves crashed into California’s coastline. Offshore National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration buoys recorded wave heights of greater than 30ft (9 metres) last Friday. The Monterey, California, buoy recorded a wave height of 34.1ft, which would make it the highest reading in 30 years. Coastal warnings extended from last weekend through this week, with alerts extending until Friday night.

stories.title: More climate money for Africa? Europe says use what's already pledged
stories.summary: Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Africa is pushing for adaptation finance to be tripled by 2035, from an annual $40bn (Â£30bn) By Navin Singh Khadka Environmental correspondent, BBC World Service Published 20 November 2026 In Uganda's northern Karamoja region, Elijah Lobur and his family now eat just one meal a day. A severe drought that began in April has destroyed crops, while food brought in from elsewhere has become increasingly unaffordable. "Seven months without rain has brought us to this point where we now live in hunger," the 44-year-old farmer, who lives with his grandmother, wife and five children, told the BBC. "Even some of the wild plants that we used to eat have withered and dried up." Local officials say more than 90% of crops have failed in the region, where agriculture is largely rain-fed. Further south, in Malawi, Mathews Nkhambala has experienced the devastating effects of flooding. In April 2024, barely a year after Tropical Cyclone Freddy devastated the country's southern region, floods displaced people in Chikwawa district. Nkhambala fled to higher ground with his wife and four children as floodwaters swept through his village. "As we reached a safe height, we saw our house swept away right in front of our eyes.
